first.rationale: Two of three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) map directly onto the onboarding/activation lever, which has two independent supporting memories (memory_86, memory_31) suggesting a durable, low-risk lift in completion and downstream activation. The competitor pricing pressure creates strong temptation toward promotional_pricing (memory_73), but that memory's summary speaks only to acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive segments, not to long-term qualified-revenue quality or retention/margin effects, and reactive discounting against an aggressive competitor risks attracting low-LTV accounts and eroding sustainable revenue. Since only one experiment slot is available, I'm prioritizing the onboarding fix (broader relevance to two live metrics, less downside risk) over a reactive pricing match, but I want to verify the original source records for memory_86 (to confirm effect size/durability before committing the week's only slot) and memory_73 (to check whether the archived record flagged any retention or margin risk that the consolidated summary omitted, since that materially affects whether pricing should be reconsidered next cycle). Scale is set to standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because activation/onboarding metrics have shifted recently and prior lift may not fully generalize to current conditions, and rather than small_guarded_test because two corroborating memories give reasonable confidence to run a normal-sized test.
